Message

From the Metropolitan

Northeast American Diocese

His Grace Zachariah Mar Nicholovos

Metropolitan, Northeast American Diocese
Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church

Blessings to our Vicar and faithful of Saint Gregorios Orthodox Church of Bensalem, Pennsylvania!

Dearly beloved,

It is with thanksgiving to Almighty God that we offer our prayers, and best wishes upon our parish as the community celebrates her Golden Jubilee. Fifty years in the life of a parish is a remarkable milestone, bearing witness to the unwavering faithfulness of God and the steadfast dedication of generations of believers. We remember with profound gratitude the pioneering clergy and faithful whose vision, sacrifices, and commitment laid the foundation for this spiritual home. Their devotion to the Holy Church, and love for the Orthodox Christian faith, have borne abundant fruit.

A parish is more than a place of worship. It is a spiritual family, where the faithful encounter the living God through the Holy Qurbana, grow in holiness through prayer and repentance, and bear witness to His love through service to one another and the wider community. For five decades, St. Gregorios Orthodox Church has served as such a spiritual home, preserving faith while proclaiming the timeless Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ in this land.

We take this opportunity to remember with gratitude Very Reverend K. Mathai Chor Episcopos of Blessed Memory, Reverend Geevarghese Remban, the other esteemed clergy, founding members, benefactors, and all those who have labored faithfully throughout these fifty years. Their prayers, and sacrifice, are an enduring part of the spiritual foundation of this parish.

As we celebrate this occasion, we encourage you not only to look back with gratitude but also to look forward with renewed vision and commitment. May our parish strive to become that “city on a hill” (Matthew 5:14) as our Lord encourages us to become. We pray that our Lord will continue to bless your endeavors, deepen your unity in Christ, and strengthen your witness to truly fulfill the words of our Savior.

May the blessings and mercies of God Almighty be showered upon us all.

Yours in our Lord,
Metropolitan Zachariah Mar Nicholovos
November 5, 2026

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 21 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

Our Clergy

Rev. Fr. K. P. Varghese

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church, Bensalem

Rev. Fr. K. P. Varghese

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church, Bensalem

It is with profound joy and gratitude that I write to congratulate St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church of Bensalem, on the joyous occasion of its Golden Jubilee. This house of worship stands as a glorious testament to God's presence and a beautiful expression of His love for the community.

While I was the Vicar of St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church of Baltimore, I was familiar with this Church. My connection with this parish deepened when our daughter, Ceena Mathew, began her service as Associate Minister in 2023. Following my retirement as Vicar of the Baltimore church, my visits became more frequent. Upon relocating to Pennsylvania in 2024, I was blessed to become an active participant in the life of this church. The Vicar Fr. Shibu Mathai and the parish community welcomed us with open arms—a warmth that continues to sustain us till today. I am particularly thankful to the church for lovingly honoring my own Golden Jubilee of Priestly Ordination on November 1, 2025.

As the parish celebrates its own 50-year milestone in 2026, I express my heartfelt appreciation to the dedicated Vicar, Shibu Achen, for his faithful pastoral care, to the dedicated Church Managing Committee, and to all the parishioners for their love, unity and cooperation. We offer our prayers that Almighty God continues to shower abundant blessings upon this parish.

May this Golden Jubilee serve as a grateful remembrance of the grace received in the past and a renewed commitment to our shared future. I wish every family the choicest blessings of our Heavenly Father. May the intercession of our patron saint, St. Gregorios of Parumala, remain a fortress of faith for us all.

Rev. Fr. K. P. Varghese

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 22 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

Our Clergy

Jubilee: A Sacred Journey of God’s Faithfulness

Associate Minister

Mrs. Ceena Mathew

Associate Minister
St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church

There are moments in the life of a church when we are invited to pause—not merely to count the years, but to remember the prayers that sustained us, the hands that labored, and the generations that carried the faith forward. A Jubilee is such a moment.

In Leviticus 25, God established the Jubilee as a sacred time of restoration, freedom, and new beginnings. At its heart was this profound reminder: “The land is Mine; for you are strangers and sojourners with Me” (Leviticus 25:23). Jubilee reminds us that everything we possess is entrusted to us by God, and every blessing ultimately comes from Him. The biblical Jubilee was more than a festival. It was a declaration of God's sovereignty, a restoration of relationships, and a reminder that His people were called to live with justice, compassion, and trust in Him.

As we celebrate our parish Jubilee, we look back with grateful hearts upon a journey marked by God’s abundant grace. God has incredibly blessed our parish. Through the faith, prayers, sacrifices, and dedication of generations, He has nurtured our community in ways our founders may never have imagined. We give thanks for our clergy, families, faithful servants, children, and all who have contributed to the life of our parish. Those who planted the seeds of faith before us may no longer be physically present, but their legacy continues to bear fruit.

At the heart of our Malankara Orthodox tradition is a living faith centered on Jesus Christ and nourished through the Holy Qurbana, prayer, Scripture, and the sacramental life of the Church. We have received a precious inheritance, one that we are called not merely to preserve, but to live faithfully and pass on to future generations.

Jubilee is more than a remembrance of the past; it is an invitation to renewal. Just as the biblical Jubilee called people to restoration and a fresh beginning, may this celebration renew our commitment to Christ, strengthen our fellowship, heal divisions, and inspire us to serve one another and the wider community with love. We must also ask ourselves: What will the next generation inherit from us? Beyond buildings, programs, and accomplishments, may they inherit a vibrant faith, a spirit of prayer, a heart for service, and a deep love for the Holy Church.

As we celebrate this milestone, let us look back with gratitude, live in the present with faith, and look toward the future with hope. The God who has faithfully guided and richly blessed our parish will continue to lead us in the years ahead.

The years are our history. Faith is our inheritance. The future is our responsibility. And every blessing is a testimony to the faithfulness of God.

To God alone be the glory.
Ceena Mathew

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 23 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

The Beginnings

In the Words of Rev. Fr. Dr. Paul Varki • Co-Founder

Rev. Fr. Dr. Paul Varki

Co-Founder • St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church

A first-person account of the parish's earliest days, written by the deacon who hosted Philadelphia's pioneering ecumenical Orthodox worship and petitioned the Catholicos for the first parish kalpana.

In the summer of 1965, some of us who were working and studying in Philadelphia and surrounding areas got together and planned a worship service of different denominations, including the Malankara Orthodox Church. Fr. Dr. K. M. Simon and Fr. A. T. Abraham were early celebrants of the Orthodox Holy Qurbana, and I was the deacon who assisted and hosted those priests. In addition, the late H. G. Mar Makarios (then Fr. K. C. Thomas), the late H. G. Mar Theodosious (then Fr. P. T. Punnoose, who was my dear friend from my old seminary days), the late Rev. Fr. John Mathews, Very Rev. Fr. Cherian Neelankal, and Very Rev. Fr. Yohannan Sankarathil were some of the other priests who conducted the Holy Qurbana in the beginning.

The Orthodox Qurbana was conducted once a month at Asbury Church, which was given to us rent-free. In those days we had Marthoma, Catholic, CSI, and other denominational members who attended the services. These services were opened to all. Thus, in Philadelphia — the City of Brotherly Love — the vineyard which St. Thomas, our founding father and disciple of Jesus, started in Odessa, was born.

After each Sunday service we got together in someone's residence for lunch and fellowship. This went on for eleven years. After awhile, some groups separated and started their own worship service in the seventies. I contacted Bishop Ogylby of the Episcopal Church, who [gave us his] Cathedral and chapel rent-free for Qurbana [at] 38th and Chestnut Streets. We also started our own service and Qurbana, which Rev. Fr. K. Mathai (now V. Rev. Fr. K. Mathai) kindly conducted. The first Diocesan Bishop, H. G. Mar Makarios — founder of the American Diocese — appointed him as Vicar in 1979.

Before Mathai Achen came to Philadelphia as Vicar, I sent an application to the Catholicos H. H. Baselios Marthoma Mathews I (who was not only my teacher at M. D. Seminary, but my benefactor), and His Holiness sent me a kalpana authorizing a parish in Philadelphia. It was on the basis of that kalpana of authorization that Mathai Achen was appointed Vicar by H. G. Mar Makarios, and the kalpana was read by Very Rev. Fr. K. Mathai in the church. After H. G. Mar Makarios came and inaugurated the American Diocese, the St. Thomas Orthodox Church — the first Orthodox church in Philadelphia — came into being. This is now St. Gregorios.

The beginnings still go through the currents of our souls — the earliest settlers in Philadelphia. May the patron Saint, Mar Gregorios, whose memory we cherish, bless this elegant church in Bensalem, PA, which is the outcome of the dedicated and courageous people of our beloved church.

Reprinted from a previous SGMOC souvenir publication. Bracketed text indicates words obscured by the original page binding.

A Tribute to Rev. Fr. Dr. Paul Varki

Rev. Fr. Dr. Paul Varki (formerly Dn. Paul Varki) faithfully served the Malankara Orthodox Church throughout his life. As we celebrate our Golden Jubilee, we lovingly remember a man whose devotion, humility, and steadfast service shaped the earliest foundations of our community.

Ordained as a deacon at age 18 by His Holiness Baselios Geevarghese II, he came to the United States in 1957 for higher studies. He pursued advanced academic work—including studies at Princeton University—and later earned a doctorate in Psychology. While serving as a Board-certified Psychologist for the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, he quietly nurtured the spiritual life of Malayalee Orthodox Christians in the region.

In 1965, he helped organize monthly worship at Asbury Church, hosting clergy from multiple denominations. This ecumenical fellowship became a spiritual home for Orthodox, Marthoma, Catholic, CSI, and other Kerala Christians for eleven years.

A turning point came in 1976, when he invited Rev. Fr. K. Mathai to lead Holy Week services. The overwhelming response led to the formation of the first Orthodox parish in Philadelphia. He later wrote to the Catholicos requesting authorization for a parish—resulting in the establishment of St. Thomas Orthodox Church of India (STOCI) on October 10, 1976.

The parish grew steadily, acquiring its first church building in Torresdale in 1984 and later building a new church in Bensalem, consecrated in 2009. As the new church neared completion, Paul Varki Achen reflected on the community’s journey with a joyful Malayalam poem:

അറുപത്തിനാലിൽ വിശ്വാസികൾ നട്ട മുന്തിരി വെസ്റ്റ് ഫിലിയിൽ
സെൻറ്‌ തോമസ് ആയി വന്നെല്ലോ
അതിനെ നനച്ചു വളർത്തി നാം സെൻറ്‌ ഗ്രീഗോറിയോസ് ആയി
ടോറസ്ഡെയിലിൽ ശോഭിച്ചു
[വീണ്ടും] ചേരുക നീ എൻ മാനസമേ
ബെൻസലേമിലെ നിലയത്തിൽ
പരുമല മരുവും തിരുമേനി വന്നു വസിക്കുന്നീ നാളിൽ
ഇന്നീ ജനന പെരുന്നാളിൽ

Rev. Fr. Dr. Paul Varki’s legacy is one of faithfulness, perseverance, and love. He helped build a community before there was a parish, welcomed clergy before there was a resident priest, and fostered unity long before there were church buildings. His memory remains a blessing to every Orthodox family in Greater Philadelphia.

— Mariamma Varki

Our Story

Our community traces its origins to 1962, when Fr. K. M. Simon celebrated the first Malayalam service in Dr. T. V. Philip's apartment on Pine Street, Philadelphia. After fourteen years of ecumenical Sunday worship, the parish was officially founded in October 1976 by V. Rev. Kaleeckal Mathai Cor Episcopos — first as St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church, with the Holy Qurbana celebrated at the Church of the Savior Cathedral chapel, 38th & Chestnut Streets.

In 1984, following parish reorganization, our community was reconstituted as St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church — in honor of St. Geevarghese Gregorios of Parumala, the first Indian saint of the Orthodox Church. Fr. K. Mathai continued as Vicar.

A 1994 attempt to build on Verree Road was prevented by zoning. In 1995 the parish purchased its first permanent home at 7721 Torresdale Avenue, Philadelphia. Land at 4136 Hulmeville Road, Bensalem was acquired in 2005 (with adjacent property added in 2006); the new church was first occupied on Christmas Day 2008 and consecrated May 22–23, 2009.

In 2011, our parish hosted the historic Metropolitan Enthronement of His Grace Zachariah Mar Nicholovos, attended by over one thousand faithful. Rev. Fr. Shibu Venad Mathai was appointed Vicar that same year, continuing to lead our vibrant community.

Honoring the Past • Empowering the Present

In Memoriam

Proof copy

V. Rev. Kaleeckal Mathai Cor Episcopos

July 3, 1942 – October 12, 2023

Founding Vicar • St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church

❖

A visionary spiritual leader and devoted shepherd, Very Rev. Kaleeckal Mathai Cor Episcopos played a foundational role in establishing and nurturing the Malankara Orthodox community in Philadelphia. From his early calling to the priesthood, he dedicated his life to the Church, guiding the congregation through its formative years, growth, and the establishment of a permanent home in Bensalem. His unwavering faith, humility, compassion, and tireless dedication continue to inspire all of us.

Ordained as a deacon in 1974 and to the priesthood in 1975, he served as the Founding Vicar of St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church from 1976 to 2011. In 1996, he was elevated to Cor Episcopos and also served the Northeast American Diocese as a Diocesan Council Member and Clergy Secretary.

❖

May his blessed memory be eternal.

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 33 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

In Memoriam

Proof copy

Rev. Fr. Dr. Paul Varki

February 7, 1931 – March 26, 2014

Pioneer • Spiritual Leader • Faithful Servant

❖

Rev. Fr. Dr. Paul Varki was a pioneering spiritual leader whose dedication helped lay the foundation for Malankara Orthodox worship in the Philadelphia region. Beginning in 1965, he played an instrumental role in bringing Orthodox Christians together for worship, fostering an ecumenical fellowship that eventually contributed to the establishment of the parish in 1976.

After obtaining his Master of Divinity degree from Princeton Theological Seminary, he pursued further studies in psychology, earning his doctorate. His academic accomplishments complemented his spiritual calling, reflecting his lifelong commitment to faith, education, and service.

Through his vision, leadership, and tireless efforts, Fr. Paul Varki helped nurture the early Orthodox community in Philadelphia. His contributions remain an important part of the history of St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church and the spiritual heritage of generations who followed.

❖

May his blessed memory be eternal.

Mariamma Varki and Family

❖

Dn. Markose Mani was a devoted servant of God and a faithful deacon of St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church. With a humble heart and unwavering faith, he faithfully served the Church and its community for many years, supporting the growth of the parish through his dedication, love, and quiet leadership.

Known for his gentle spirit, kindness, and deep commitment to the Church, Dn. Markose played an important role in the spiritual and communal life of our parish. His faithful presence, service at the altar, and care for the parish family touched many lives and remain an inspiration to all of us.

We remember him with deep gratitude for his life of service and the lasting legacy he leaves in our hearts.

St. Joseph's Forum

Brothers in Christ • Faith • Fellowship

About

St. Joseph's Forum is the men's fellowship ministry of St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church, named in honor of St. Joseph, the earthly father of our Lord Jesus Christ. Rooted in the spiritual leadership exemplified by St. Joseph, the Forum brings together the men of SGMOC in prayer, service, and faith formation.

The ministry focuses on spiritual growth, biblical study, mentorship of young men in the faith, and communal service projects. Through regular gatherings and events, St. Joseph's Forum strengthens the bonds of Christian brotherhood and inspires men to be leaders in their homes, parish, and communities.

St. Joseph's Forum

Friendship • Fellowship • Faith

Brothers in Christ, Serving Our Parish

Originally established in 2024 as the SGMOC Men's Forum, the organization was formally renamed to honor St. Joseph — a timeless pillar of quiet strength, humility, and obedience. Throughout 2025 and 2026, our members have actively immersed themselves in the sacramental life and service of the church, providing volunteer support for the Jubilee Celebrations, the annual Church Picnic, Parish Day, the Volleyball Tournament, the Harvest Festival, the Parish Perunnal, and Christmas programs.

Executive Committee 2024–2026

Lead: Paul Maret • Secretary: Sumod Abraham • Treasurer: Nithin Maret • Mission Board Representative: Ajo Maret

Committee Members: Biju Mani, John Kappil, Saji Thomas, Biju Chacko, Reji Ninan, Santhosh Ninan, Shiju Poovathoor, Mathew Joseph

Spiritual leadership: Rev. Fr. Shibu V. Mathai (Vicar), Mrs. Ceena Mathew (Associate Minister), Rev. Fr. K. P. Varghese

Activities & Spiritual Growth

Sunday meetings and seminars. Monthly meetings follow the Holy Qurbana and fellowship lunch. Sessions have included a Family Communication Series (Rev. Fr. Shibu V. Mathai and Mrs. Ceena Mathew), Cyber Security Awareness (Reji Ninan, Sumod Abraham, Saji Thomas), an Introduction to Artificial Intelligence (Sumod Abraham, James Varghese, Alisha Maret), and Finance, Investment and Retirement Planning (Biju Mani, Reji Ninan, Saji Thomas, Joseph Abraham).

Honoring our members. On November 16, 2025, the Forum celebrated Rev. Fr. K. P. Varghese on the 50th anniversary of his Holy Priesthood. On December 21, 2025, we celebrated the 90th birthday of our most senior member, Mr. Kuruvilla Kallelil. On March 22, 2026, the Forum honored Mr. Varkey Vattakkattu and Mrs. Mercy Varkey upon their relocation to Dallas, Texas.

Care and Share Ministry. Coordinated by John Kappil and Paul Maret, this ministry arranges home visits to parish members unable to attend services due to illness or age.

Fellowship and recreation. Annual urban hiking trips to New York City in 2025 and 2026 (coordinated by Biju Chacko and Mathew Joseph), a summer social gathering of over 30 members on August 23, 2025 (Nithin Ipe and Shiju Poovathoor), and performances at the Ecumenical and SGMOC Christmas programs.

— Submitted by Paul Maret, SJ Forum Lead (2024–2026)

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 42 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

Good Samaritan Mission

Love God in Prayer • Serve God by Caring & Sharing

About

The Good Samaritan Mission (GSM) was established in 2016 under the leadership of Rev. Fr. Shibu V. Mathai, with approximately 25+ active members. GSM is a fellowship of elderly and retired faithful of SGMOC, dedicated to caring for those who are physically isolated, emotionally distressed, or spiritually in need.

Ministry Activities: Weekly family visits featuring Bible readings, singing, prayer, and shared meals. GSM also leads Lenten prayers, hosts seasonal gatherings including Onam feasts and Christmas celebrations, and provides financial assistance to those in need.

Community Engagement: GSM actively partners with local organizations on service projects. In 2026, the mission coordinated with the Department of Public Works on a community improvement initiative involving volunteer scouts and skilled laborers, working on landscaping, paving, and facility enhancements with support from local partnerships.

Good Samaritan Mission

ദൈവ നാമത്തിനു മഹത്വം

കഴിഞ്ഞ പത്തു വർഷമായി നമ്മുടെ ഇടവകയിൽ പ്രവർത്തിച്ചു വരുന്ന ഒരു ആത്മീക പ്രസ്ഥാനം ആണ് Good Samaritan Mission. എല്ലാ വ്യാഴാഴ്ചകളിലും രാവിലെ പത്തു മണിമുതൽ ഞങ്ങൾ പ്രാർത്ഥനകൂട്ടമായി കൂടിവരുന്നു. ചില പ്രത്യേക സാഹചര്യങ്ങളിൽ മാത്രമേ ഈ കൂട്ടായ്മക്ക് മുടക്കം ഉണ്ടായിട്ടുള്ളൂ. ഈ കൂട്ടയ്മയിൽ വേദ പുസ്തകത്തിൽ നിന്നും പുതിയ നിയമവും പഴയ നിയമവും എല്ലാവരും വായിക്കുകയും, വചനം പഠിക്കുകയും ചെയ്യും. ഞങ്ങൾ വേദപുസ്തകം മുഴുവനും ഒരു പ്രാവശ്യം വായിച്ചു കഴിഞ്ഞു. ഇനിയും തുടർന്നു കൊണ്ടിരിക്കുന്നു. സാഹചര്യം അനുസരിച്ചുള്ള വിവരണങ്ങളും പൊരുളുകളും ഷിബു അച്ചനും സീനാ മാത്യു വും വിസിറ്റ് ചെയ്യുന്ന തിരുമേനിമാരും അച്ചന്മാരും വിശദീകരിച്ചു തരും.

നമ്മുടെ അറിവിലും അല്ലാതെയുമുള്ള അനേകരുടെ വിവിധങ്ങളായ ആവശ്യങ്ങൾക്കുവേണ്ടി പ്രാർത്ഥിക്കുന്നത് വളരെ അനുഗ്രഹമാണ്.

ഈ കൂട്ടായ്മയിൽ കൂടി പല വിധത്തിലുള്ള സഹായങ്ങൾ പലർക്കും നാട്ടിൽ ചെയ്യുവാൻ ദൈവം സഹായിച്ചു. ഈ സഹായങ്ങൾ തുടർന്നു കൊണ്ടു പോകുവാൻ ദൈവം അനുവദിക്കട്ടെ എന്ന് പ്രാർത്ഥിക്കുന്നു.

ഷിബു അച്ചൻ്റെ അനുവാദത്തോടുകൂടി ഞങ്ങൾ പലപ്പോഴും ഞങ്ങളുടെ അനുഭവ സാക്ഷ്യങ്ങൾ പങ്കുവെച്ചിട്ടുണ്ട്. "ജീവിതം നമ്മളെ എന്തൊക്കെ പഠിപ്പിച്ചു; നമ്മൾ എന്തെല്ലാം പഠിച്ചു"എന്നുള്ള ഒരു വിഷയം അച്ചൻ ഞങ്ങൾക്ക് തന്നു. എല്ലാവർക്കും ഓരോ ആഴ്ച്ച ഇതിനെക്കുറിച്ചു അവതരിപ്പിക്കാൻ അവസരം അനുവദിച്ചു. പലരും ഈ വിഷയം അവതരിപ്പിച്ചപ്പോൾ പുതിയ അറിവുകളും അനുഭവങ്ങളും വളരെ ലഭിക്കുവാൻ സാധിച്ചു.

ഒരു സാധാരണ കർഷക കുടുംബത്തിൽ അഞ്ചു മക്കളിൽ രണ്ടാമനായ എനിക്കുണ്ടായ അനുഭവങ്ങൾ പറയുവാൻ സാധിച്ചു. രാവിലെ അഞ്ചു മണിക്ക് പ്രാർത്ഥിക്കാൻ താമസിച്ചു പോയാൽ തണുത്ത വെള്ളം തലയിൽ ഒഴിക്കുക എന്ന ശിക്ഷ ലഭിച്ചിട്ടുണ്ട്. അന്ന് പിതാവിനോട് ദേഷ്യം മനസ്സിൽ തോന്നിയത് വളരെ തെറ്റാണെന്നു ഇപ്പോൾ തോന്നുന്നു.

പ്രാർത്ഥന: എപ്പോഴും പ്രാര്ഥനയോടു കൂടി തുടക്കം കുറിക്കണം എന്നുള്ള ഉപദേശം പിതാവിൽ നിന്നും പഠിച്ചു.

St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church 44 Golden Jubilee 1976 – 2026

Good Samaritan Mission

അച്ചടക്കം: ഞാൻ പഠിച്ച സ്കൂളിൽ അര മണിക്കൂർ വേദ പഠനം ക്രിസ്ത്യൻ കുട്ടികൾക്ക് നിർബന്ധമായിരുന്നു. അഞ്ചു മിനിറ്റ് എല്ലാ കുട്ടികളും പിൻ-ഡ്രോപ്പ് സൈലെൻസിൽ ആയിരിക്കണം എന്നുള്ളത് തെറ്റിയാൽ ശിക്ഷ വളരെ കഠിനമായിരുന്നു.

അനുസരണം: സ്കൂൾ പ്രധാന റോഡിൽ നിന്നും വളരെ ഉയരത്തിൽ ആയിരുന്നു, പരുപരുത്ത കാട്ടു കല്ലു കൊണ്ട് നിർമ്മിച്ച വഴിയിൽകൂടി ഓടി ഇറങ്ങരുത് എന്നുള്ള പിതാവിൻ്റെ കർശന ഉപദേശത്തെ അനുസരിക്കാതെ എപ്പോഴും ഓടി ഇറങ്ങുമായിരുന്നു. കാൽ തെറ്റി ഒരു പ്രാവശ്യം മുകളിൽ നിന്നും ശയന പ്രദക്ഷിണം നടത്തി പ്രധാന റോഡിൽ വന്നു വീണപ്പോൾ ശരീരത്തിൻ്റെ പല ഭാഗത്തും തൊലി നഷ്ടപെട്ടിരുന്നു. രണ്ടു കൂട്ടുകാർ താങ്ങി എടുത്തു കൊണ്ട് ഭവനത്തിൽ വന്നപ്പോൾ പിതാവിൻ്റെ ശിക്ഷ അതിലും വേദനാത്മകമായിരുന്നു. തെറ്റു കണ്ടാൽ ശിക്ഷിക്കാനും തിരുത്താനും അയൽക്കാരും പരിചയക്കാരും ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നതു കാരണം പല തെറ്റുകളിൽ നിന്നും ഒഴിഞ്ഞിരിക്കാൻ സാധിച്ചു.

പുതിയ നിയമത്തിൽ ന്യായശാസ്ത്രിയും കർത്താവും തമ്മിലുള്ള സംഭാഷണത്തിൻ്റെ ഒടുവിൽ കർത്താവു അവനോടു പറയുന്നു "നീ ദൈവരാജ്യത്തിൽ നിന്നും അകന്നവനല്ല."ദൈവരാജ്യത്തിൽ പ്രവേശിക്കണമെങ്കിൽ പ്രാര്ഥനയെന്ന താക്കോൽ ആവശ്യമാണ്. നമ്മുടെ എല്ലാവരുടേയും കൈവശമുള്ള ഈ താക്കോൽ വേണ്ട സമയത്തു ഉപയോഗിച്ചില്ലാ എങ്കിൽ അകത്തു പ്രവേശിക്കാൻ കഴിയാത്ത കന്യകമാരെ പോലെ ആയിത്തീരും.

നമ്മുടെ കർത്താവു കുരിശിൽ മരിച്ചു ഉയർത്തെഴുന്നേറ്റു നമുക്ക് ഭവനം ഒരുക്കുവാൻ സ്വർഗ്ഗത്തിലേക്ക് പോയിരിക്കുകയാണ്. നമ്മളെ ചേർക്കുവാൻ വേഗം വരുന്നു. അതിൻ്റെ എല്ലാ ലക്ഷണങ്ങളും കണ്ടു കഴിഞ്ഞു. സമയം ഇനിയും അധികമില്ല. മനസാന്തരപ്പെടുവിൻ. നമ്മുടെ തെറ്റുകൾ ദൈവസന്നിധിൽ ഏറ്റു പറഞ്ഞു പാപ ക്ഷമ പ്രാപിച്ചു ദൈവത്തോടു നിരന്നു കൊൾവീൻ.

നമ്മുടെ ഇടവകയുടെ അൻപതാം വാർഷീകം ആഘോഷിക്കുന്ന ഈ സമയത്തു GSM ൻ്റെ എല്ലാവിധ ആശംസകളും പ്രാർത്ഥനയും അർപ്പിക്കുന്നു.

പ്രാർത്ഥനയോടുകൂടി

— John Varghese, GSM Coordinator

Our Choir

Serving God through music and worship

“Sing to the Lord a new song; sing to the Lord, all the earth.”

— Psalm 96:1

The Church Choir Ministry is a dedicated group of Orthodox believers who use their God-given musical talents to glorify God, lead the congregation, and enhance the worship experience. As an essential part of our Orthodox tradition, the choir helps create an atmosphere that draws the congregation closer to God’s presence during the Divine Liturgy.

Orthodox tones and musical settings are among the most beautiful in the world. As choir members, we honor God with humility and dedication, creating an uplifting atmosphere through well-sung hymns during Holy Qurbana that encourages worshippers to deeply immerse themselves in the liturgy.

Our mission is to glorify God with our voices. Beyond the beauty of the music, we aim to convey the deeper meaning of what is sung to lead the congregation in meaningful worship. We invite everyone to join us in enriching the spiritual life of our SGMOC community.

Community Outreach

Building Bridges in Bensalem

Community Partnership

Since relocating to Bensalem, SGMOC has been an active partner in the local community. Our parish is committed to serving not only our members but also our neighbors, living out the Gospel's call to love and serve all people.

We are proud members of Building a Better Bensalem (B3T), joining with other faith communities and organizations in collaborative service projects, community improvement initiatives, and interfaith fellowship.

Key Initiatives

Bensalem Unity 5K — Organized and conducted in 2016, 2017, and 2019. Our parish community participated to promote wellness and unity among all residents.

Unity Prayer Fellowship — Since 2018, we host and participate in the annual Unity Week celebrations, bringing together faith communities for prayer and fellowship.

Ecumenical Events — Active participants in World Day of Prayer, Choir Fest, interfaith gatherings, and diocesan community events.

A Journey of Faith,
Love, and Gratitude

Over the years, SGMOC has played a crucial role in our lives, nurturing our faith and guiding us along our spiritual journey. We have celebrated many joyful milestones together and have also faced our share of challenges along the way. Throughout these years, we have grown to cherish the blessing of having a loving and supportive church family, whose presence has been especially meaningful during challenging times.

We are deeply thankful for all the love, prayers, guidance, and support we have received from clergy, especially Mathai Achen, Shibu Achen, and the entire SGMOC family. Their care and spiritual guidance, together with the friendship and fellowship of our parish community, have been a source of strength and encouragement to our family.

As we happily celebrate SGMOC’s Golden Jubilee, we give thanks to God for the many blessings, treasured memories, and lasting friendships that have been such a meaningful part of our lives. May God continue to shower His blessings upon our parish, guide us in our journey, strengthen the bonds of faith and fellowship among us, and unite us as one community for generations to come.

The Sign of the Cross:
A Prayer in Every Moment

By Jonathan Chacko

Have you ever wondered why we make the Sign of the Cross before meals, when setting out on a journey, or before going to bed? The Sign of the Cross is one of the shortest and most meaningful prayers which symbolizes the Crucifixion and Resurrection of Jesus Christ. It reminds us of God’s constant presence, love, and protection in our lives.

We should make it a habit to make the Sign of the Cross not only before important events, but every significant moment in our daily lives. It serves as a reminder to place our trust in God and seek His guidance and protection as we face life’s challenges. It also reminds us of His promise to remain with us and guide us away from evil.

Whenever we make the Sign of the Cross, we should also remember those who are less fortunate, offer prayers for them, and give thanks to God for the countless blessings in our own lives. The Sign of the Cross should never be made out of habit or casually. It should always be made with reverence, faith, and a sincere understanding of its meaning.

Our family moved to Philadelphia from India in 1990. At that time, our family consisted of my wife, Rachel, our daughter Marina, and myself, Varughese. That same year, we joined SGMOC, which was worshipping at the Church of the Savior on 38th and Chestnut Streets. Mathai Achen and the church family welcomed us wholeheartedly and made us feel at home.

I have served as an Acolyte since 1968, having been ordained by the late Thoma Mar Dionysius of Niranam. After joining SGMOC, I continued this ministry and have been blessed with many opportunities to serve the Church, including multiple terms on the Board of Directors, Church Treasurer, Diocesan Assembly Member, and currently as a Malankara Association Member.

Our two younger daughters, Marilyn and Rosilyn, were both baptized at the Chestnut Street church and all three were actively involved in church life through the choir, Youth League, Sunday School, and other activities. My wife, Rachel, has also been a dedicated member of MMVS.

We are deeply grateful to God for the many blessings and opportunities He has given our family to worship, serve, and grow within this church community. As we celebrate 50 years of the Church's presence in Philadelphia, we give thanks for God's guidance and for the intercession of St. Mary, St. Thomas, and St. Gregorios. We pray for continued blessings upon our Church and its members for generations to come.

Jinu John & Family

When many of us came to the United States of America from Kerala, we brought with us more than dreams and hopes for a better future. We also brought our culture, traditions, memories, and most importantly, the Orthodox faith that was passed down to us by our parents and grandparents. It is the faith we grew up with, the faith that has guided us through different stages of our lives, and the faith we now hope to pass on to our children.

Starting a life in a new country came with many changes and challenges. Through it all, we are grateful that we have been able to continue living and growing in our Malankara Orthodox faith. Through SGMOC, we found more than a church. We found a spiritual home and a community where we could pray together, celebrate together, and support one another. Over the years, this parish has become an important part of our life and our journey here in America.

One of the greatest blessings for us as parents is seeing our children grow up in this same faith. It brings us joy to see them attend Sunday School, participate in Holy Qurbana and church celebrations, and spend time with their church friends. Through these experiences, they are learning about God, our faith, and the traditions that have been part of our families for generations. At the same time, they are building friendships and creating memories that we hope they will carry with them throughout their lives.

As SGMOC celebrates 50 years, we are especially grateful for those who came before us. Their faith, hard work, and sacrifices gave families like ours a place to call our spiritual home. They passed this faith on to us, and now it is our turn to pass it on to our children. Our hope and prayer is that they will carry it with them wherever life takes them and, one day, pass it on to the generations that follow.

Another special blessing was celebrating the 50th anniversary of Varghese Achen’s priesthood at SGMOC in November 2025.

We are thankful to the parish community for welcoming us and we are especially grateful to Shibu Achen for inviting us to serve alongside him in the ministries of the church and for giving us the opportunity to be part of this wonderful parish family. As we continue this journey together, we look forward to growing in Christ through the sacramental life of the Church, through service, and through the fellowship and love we share with one another. May the intercession of St. Gregorios of Parumala and the abundant grace of our Lord Jesus Christ continue to guide and bless SGMOC for generations to come.

Jiji Koshy & Family

Golden Jubilee Family Sponsor
Proof copy

Jiji Koshy was born in the early 1960s and raised in Vazhoor, Kottayam, Kerala, as the youngest of eight children. His family was active in St. Peter’s Malankara Syrian Orthodox Church in Pulikkalkavala. After earning a degree in Business and Administration and working as a Logistics Manager in Kerala, Jiji immigrated to the United States in 1991, settling in New Jersey with his eldest brother, George.

Beena Abraham was born in the late 1960s and raised in North Paravur, Ernakulam, the second of three children of Areekal Abraham Tharian and Vazhappilli Sucy Abraham. After earning a master’s degree in physics, Beena married Jiji in 1992. Jiji settled in Philadelphia with his brother Thomas, where he helped establish St. Mary’s Malankara Syrian Orthodox Church; Beena and their daughter Jane joined him in 1996.

In the summer of 2000, a season of change — a new job, a new home, their eldest starting kindergarten and a third child on the way — brought them to St. Gregorios, shortly before Joanne was born. Over the years both became active in the ministries, and their daughters in the Youth League and Sunday School. In 2023 Beena made parish history as the first woman to serve as Treasurer and Trustee.

Jiji grew up serving at the altar in his home parish, and after immigrating faced pressure from colleagues and family to join other denominations. He stayed with the faith handed down to him, and encourages those around him to do the same. Beena set out to be a physicist and found instead a profession in computers; leaving her family in Kerala, she built a new one here, and came to find in SGMOC a second home.

Jiji established and runs Alma Digital Vision, his photography and videography business, and Beena works as an Enterprise Systems Programmer with the City of Philadelphia. Their daughters have gone on to science research, engineering, literature and writing. Above all the family treasures the church community that has carried and enriched their lives.

Allen Kuruvila & Family

A journey that began with a baptism and grew into a beautiful sense of faith, friendship, and belonging

When we moved to New Jersey in 2020, the world looked very different. The pandemic had brought life to a standstill, and being new to the area, we were searching not only for a church but also for a community where our family could feel at home.

During that time, a priest from the West Coast told us about St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church, Bensalem. Since we were also thinking about having our little one baptized, he encouraged us to reach out to the church. That recommendation turned out to be the beginning of a beautiful journey for our family.

When we first approached our Parish Vicar, Rev. Fr. Shibu Venad Mathai (Shibu Achen), he welcomed us with incredible warmth and kindness. When he learned that we had moved from Mumbai, he immediately began introducing us to other Hindi-speaking families in the parish. It was a simple gesture, but for a family that was new to the area, it meant so much. The Managing Committee and the entire church community welcomed us so wholeheartedly that, from the very beginning, we felt that we belonged.

In October 2020, during a time when gatherings were still very limited, we had the blessing of baptizing our little one at St. Gregorios. With only a small number of parish members and a few of our extended family present, the baptism was held under the guidance of Rev. Fr. Shibu Venad Mathai and Very Rev. K. Mathai Cor Episcopos. Though it was a small gathering, it remains one of the most meaningful memories of our family's journey with the church.

From that day forward, St. Gregorios has become much more than the church we attend on Sundays—it has become our extended family. Our children were welcomed into Sunday School, and we were given opportunities to become involved in different ministries, cultural programs, and church activities. Through these experiences, we have met so many wonderful people, built beautiful friendships, and created memories that we will always cherish.

Over the years, going to church on Sunday has naturally become an important part of our family's life. Our children look forward to Sunday School every week and, most importantly, have formed friendships that we hope will last a lifetime. As parents, it brings us great joy to see them growing up surrounded by faith, friendship, tradition, and a community that cares for them.

Looking back at how our journey began in the uncertain days of 2020, we are deeply grateful that God led us to St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church, Bensalem. The warmth with which we were welcomed continues to be something we treasure. Our parish has played a vital role in shaping our family's life, strengthening our faith, and giving us a true sense of belonging.

What began as a search for a church became the blessing of finding a church family and a home away from home.

A Statement of Faith

My wife Mariam and I have been members of SGMOC since its very inception. We came to Delaware in 1975 for our respective Residency trainings. We joined the Malayalam services soon after we arrived — at first interdenominational — followed by a fellowship lunch at someone's home for which everyone contributed a dollar. The first Orthodox services started after the arrival of Rev. Fr. K. Mathai at the Chapel of what now is the Philadelphia Episcopal Cathedral at 38th and Chestnut Streets.

We were both born into Orthodox families, she in Secunderabad, I in Malaysia, and have attended Orthodox services all our lives. I attended the M. D. Seminary Higher Secondary School in Kottayam, then the location of the Orthodox Seminary. I was an Acolyte while at the Union Christian College, Alwaye. Rev. Fr. K. K. Mathews, who went on to be Barnabas Thirumeni, was our vicar while I studied at the Christian Medical College in Vellore.

We both are very proud of SGMOC for its dynamism, spirituality, community outreach and care for the members under the leadership of Rev. Fr. Shibu V. Mathai.

— Thomas K. Mammen MD, FACS

Golden Jubilee Notes

It is with immense gratitude that we, Shobha and I, thank God for providing us the opportunity to be part of this Malankara Orthodox Church from its inception as the first parish in Philadelphia in 1976. We thank our parents for nurturing us with the zeal and love for the Orthodox Churches we were members of, from our childhood. When we immigrated to this nation of opportunities in the early 70's, we started attending the Ecumenical congregation in Philadelphia, established during the latter part of the 1960s by a good number of Malayalee Christians belonging to different denominations living in the Philadelphia metropolitan region.

1976 was a historical year for the Orthodox Church with the arrival of Rev. Fr. K. Mathai to the US and later to Philadelphia with Mariamma Kochamma and their twin girls. With his initiative, and in response to the demand from most of our Orthodox members, the first Orthodox parish with the name St. Thomas Orthodox Church of India, Philadelphia (STOCI) was established in the city of Philadelphia on the 10th of October 1976. We worshipped in the chapel of the Philadelphia Episcopal Church on 38th and Chestnut Streets. I was one of the members of the first Board of Trustees of the parish. We were also blessed with the birth of our daughter Namita in September 1976.

1984 was another important and memorable year for us. We welcomed the arrival of our twin boys Matthew and Michael. It was also the year that St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church (SGMOC) was formed after the dissolution of STOCI by His Grace Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios, Metropolitan of the American diocese. The majority of the members of the dissolved STOCI parish joined and formed the new SGMOC parish with Mathai Achen as its vicar. The parish bought a small church building on Torresdale Avenue in Philadelphia in 1995.

During the next ten years, the parish membership increased in number, and grew in prominence as one of the most vibrant parishes of the American Diocese. The need for a larger place of worship and space for other spiritual activities and amenities resulted in finding the property on Hulmeville Road in Bensalem, just outside of Philadelphia in 2005. The new SGMOC building was consecrated in May 2009. After Mathai Achen's retirement, Rev. Fr. Shibu Mathai was appointed as the vicar of SGMOC in 2011. The parish has witnessed tremendous growth in membership and spirituality under his leadership.

On a personal note, I was blessed to have had the opportunity to serve the parish as an acolyte as well as a Sunday School teacher, and also as a member in the parish administration for several years.

— Korah T. Mani

Memories of Our Early Years

As America celebrates the 250th anniversary of its independence this year, we, as early Indian immigrants, are also celebrating our church’s Golden Jubilee, our 50th anniversary. We started our congregation in 1976 with the late Very Rev. Fr. K. Mathai Corepiscopa. Our first church was at 38th and Chestnut Streets in Philadelphia, the City of Brotherly Love. As we look back, we feel fortunate to have a new church in Bensalem Township.

We faced many hardships in the beginning. My wife joined the congregation in 1976, and I joined in 1977. Every Sunday, Mathai Achen celebrated the Holy Qurbana after blessing a small table as our Altar. Afterward, we had to pack everything up and take it home. This was very difficult because we had no permanent place to worship.

We remember cold Sunday mornings when we wanted to make coffee for the congregation. We all pitched in to buy the supplies and made the coffee in the small kitchen in the basement. The priest of the 38th Street Church, Fr. Hadvick, along with the custodian, helped us use the kitchen properly.

Our small group enjoyed organizing picnics and tours to Busch Gardens and Washington, D.C. Among the people I especially remember from those days are the late Mr. M.P. Paulose and Ms. Rachel Parel, who now resides in California.

Although we were not financially secure, we wanted a place of our own. We visited many properties, but we did not always have enough support. We tried to purchase a property on Verree Road in Northeast Philadelphia, but we could not obtain zoning approval, even though we had already laid a cornerstone. We then acquired a small property in Torresdale, where we held our services until we built our current church in Bensalem.

There are too many memories to mention here. As one of the early families, we worked hard for the church. I served as Treasurer and as a member of the Board of Trustees for many years, and my wife has been a dedicated member of the MMVS. I am happy to have seen this church grow over the years, and I hope it will continue to grow for the next generation.

Today, we are thankful to God Almighty for our larger and thriving church in Bensalem. This was possible only through the hard work of a core group of members in our church. We also cannot forget our former Bishops, H.G. Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios and H.G. Mathews Mar Barnabas, along with our founding priest, the late Very Rev. Fr. K. Mathai Corepiscopa.

May the prayers of all our Patron Saints and St. Mary, Mother of God, continue to bless us.

Finally, I am grateful to the Golden Jubilee Committee for allowing some of our old memories to be published.

— V. S. Mathew

Best Compliments from Thomas Paul and Family

Members of SGMOC since 1978

Board of Trustee Member — 1994–1996

Secretary — 1995–1996

Diocesan Auditor — 1998–2002

I became a member of our church in 1978, when it was known as St. Thomas Church. Having been born and raised in the Orthodox faith, I have always cherished my connection to the Church. Over the years, I have witnessed our parish's journey from 38th and Chestnut Streets to Torresdale Avenue and finally to our beautiful church in Bensalem. Among my treasured memories are the blessings of H.G. Barnabas Thirumeni and H.G. Makarios Thirumeni, especially the blessing given to my son and other children to serve in the sanctuary. As we celebrate our Golden Jubilee, my greatest hope is that future generations will remain steadfast in the Orthodox faith, actively participate in MGOCSM, and continue to strengthen and grow our beloved parish.

— Thomas Paul

Dr. T. V. Philip & Family

Golden Jubilee Family Sponsor
Proof copy

Message from the family of Dr. T. V. and Mary Philip

The very first regular worship services in the Philadelphia area for the Malankara Orthodox Church (which at that time was still named the Syrian Orthodox Church of India) were held in an apartment at 49th & Pine in the early 1960s. This was the apartment where Dr TV Philip lived with his wife, Mary (Marykutty), and infant son, George, and eventually his younger brother, John. The priest, who Dr Philip invited regularly to Philadelphia from New York City, was Rev Fr. KM Simon (later, the Very Reverend Fr. KM Simon, Cor Episcopa. By the way, Simon Achan baptized Georgie as the very first out of the hundreds of baptisms he eventually performed in the US, before his passing in 1996). These initial worship services were ecumenical; there were just a handful of Malayalis in the entire Philadelphia area at that time, and all of them attended the services. These services were also the beginning of a long line of different locations and congregations that eventually led to the founding of the St Thomas Orthodox Church in 1976 with Rev Fr. K Mathai Achan as its vicar, (later, Very Rev. K. Mathai Cor Episcopa). Later, the parish became the St Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church in Bensalem. In 1966, the family moved to Reading PA, where Neena (now married to Chris) was born. After the move to Reading, they had to drive about 1.5 hours each way to attend regular worship services in Philadelphia. Despite the distances, and the challenges with Johnny’s severe autism, they remained fully active in many church activities, including regular attendance at the Diocese Family Conference. Dr Philip was pleased to serve for 5 years as the official Auditor of the North American Diocese under His Grace Barnabas-Thirumeni in the early 2000s. As a very happy grandfather of Nathaniel and Isaac, Dr Philip lived 90 healthy and active years, passing away in June 2014, just weeks after celebrating his 90th birthday at the church. Marykutty was well loved by church members and passed away in June 2022 at age 88. On September 13th 2026, Shibu Achan was kind enough to celebrate Johnny’s 63rd birthday and his Pioneer status at St Gregorios.

— Georgie, Johnny, Neena & Chris, Nathaniel, Isaac

James Varughese & Family

Golden Jubilee Family Sponsor

Fifty Years of Grace: The Varughese Family’s Journey of Faith and Service

As our parish celebrates its Golden Jubilee under the leadership of Rev. Fr. Shibu Venad Mathai, our family—James (Jimmy), Caroline, Andrew, and Timothy (Timmy) Varughese, together with our father, Gheevarughese Mathai (Babu)—reflects with profound gratitude on the journey that has bound us to this holy sanctuary. A pinnacle moment of this Golden Jubilee celebration was the laying on of hands of Andrew by the supreme head of the Church, H.H. Moran Mar Baselios Marthoma Mathews III, to enter the holy altar. Though our sister Jenny, her husband Sandeep, and their children Amelia and Luke relocated to Tennessee in March of this year, our spiritual roots in this parish community remain unshakeable.

Over the years, God has granted our family the privilege of serving Him at the parish, regional, and diocesan levels. From serving as OVBS Coordinator, Diocese OVBS Committee Member, Sunday School Teacher and Registrar, Youth League Treasurer, MGOCSM Council Member, Parish Committee member, and member of both the Board of Directors and Mission Board, to contributing to St. Joseph's Forum, MMVS, STG, Christmas Carol, and Gregorian Harmony, as well as serving as Acolytes at the altar, each ministry has anchored our lives more deeply in the Church.

With loving hearts, we treasure the sacred memory of our dear mother and a founding member of the parish, Annamma Gheevarughese (Kunjumol), and hold fond memories of our founding vicar, V. Rev. Fr. K. Mathai Cor-Episcopos. We also honor the revered Hierarchs who guided our path: L.L. H.G. Thomas Mar Makarios, who laid hands on Jimmy to enter the altar; L.L. H.G. Mathews Mar Barnabas, who tenderly shepherded the American Diocese during the early growth of the MGOCSM; and L.L. H.G. Zachariah Mar Theophilus, who blessed and solemnized our Holy Matrimony. May their memory be eternal.

In the midst of life's present struggles and uncertainties, holding fast to our Orthodox faith and the Holy Sacraments is not merely our tradition—it is our hope and strength. May the Almighty continue to shower His divine grace upon our parish for generations to come.
